role: Test script: checks that make_report.py stops on damaged input data.
purpose: The script runs copies of the report generator make_report.py on damaged copies of its input file facts.json. It passes when the control without damage ends with exit status 0 and each of the 10 damaged cases ends with another exit status.

main_flow.step: Create a temporary folder under `test-tmp`. Read the text of make_report.py and the content of facts.json.

Define `run`. It writes a damaged copy of the facts and a copy of the generator that reads this copy and writes its page into the temporary folder. It runs the copy, prints up to 4 of its `STOP`, `FAIL`, `NOT WRITTEN` and `wrote` lines, and returns its exit status.
Define 9 damage functions. Each changes one detail of the facts: a record removed, a rate changed, a load value changed, or a boot id changed.
Run 11 cases: the control without damage, the 9 damage functions, and one case that changes the text of the generator (a reference path that does not exist).
Print `PASS` or `FAIL` per case from the exit status. Delete the temporary folder. End with exit status 0 when every case behaved as required.

behavior_notes: The test works on copies. The damaged facts, the copies of the generator and their output pages go to a new folder under `test-tmp`, and the script deletes that folder at the end. The `assert` in line 27 stops the test when the output path of a copy was not replaced.

The verdict uses the exit status only (lines 79 and 81). The control must give 0. Each damaged case must give a value other than 0. The usage text also requires that no page is written. The script prints that fact per case (line 32), and no code tests it.
The test does not check which check of the generator found the damage. It prints up to 4 lines of the generator per case, so that a reader can see the reason.
The copy of the generator still reads FACTS.md and the raw result files from their real folders. make_report.py holds these paths as fixed text [Ref1]. So the test needs these files.

Result of a saved run: the control ended with exit status 0 and wrote its page. Each of the 10 damaged cases ended with exit status 1 and a `STOP` line, and wrote no page [Ref2]. A run of a copy of this script in a scratch folder on 2026-11-21 gave the same exit statuses and the same `STOP` lines.

Link to the rates of the report: 4 cases change one rate of facts.json, by 5 GB/s in part A and by 0.5 GB/s for the runners bwx12 and bwx. In the saved run the generator found each change when it compared the record with the raw csv rows that the record names [Ref2].

words.def: the script that writes the report page of the rerun, `whole-chip-rerun-7200.html`. Its input is facts.json.
the data file of the facts sheet FACTS.md. The script build_facts.py writes both from the raw result files. Its list `intervals` holds one record per timed interval.

one entry of the list `intervals` of facts.json: one timed interval with its data set, kernel, binary, rate (`GBps`), process key (`proc_key`), load at launch (`load1_at_launch`), boot id (`boot`) and more fields [Ref3].

the field `dataset` of a record. It names the group of runs that the record belongs to. `rerun-A`, `rerun-L`, `rerun-C` and `control-I` are the four parts of the rerun. All other names are earlier runs.
data sets of earlier runs at 8000 MT/s with the older runner bwx. B5a-rev ran the kernels in reverse order.
data set of an earlier bwx12 run at 8000 MT/s in a boot with 10 memory modules.
data set of an earlier bwx12 run at 8000 MT/s with 12 memory modules. Its boot is not the boot of the other 12-module runs at 8000 MT/s.
the read test of 2026-11-17 with 120 threads, run after the memory speed was lowered to 7200 MT/s (million transfers per second). Its parts are part A, part L, part C and control I.
the 120-thread part of the test of 2026-11-13, repeated with the same two binaries.
one bwx12 process with the kernel sequence oldread, asmread, read_nop96, read_nop256, read_1pl.
one bwx12 process with the sequence oldread, read, asmread (cfwd) or asmread, read, oldread (crev).
the part L line, started from an idle machine, twice. It was added after the first numbers were seen. It is not part of the plan fixed before the run.
the inner loop of the benchmark that reads memory. On this page "kernel" means this loop. The operating system kernel is always written "Linux kernel".
portable C code with 16 running sums. Each load is followed by an add. Its name is `read` in the binary bw_old and `oldread` in the runner bwx12.
NEON intrinsics (C functions that map to Arm vector instructions), loads only. Its name is `read` in the binary bw_new and `read` in bwx12.
a hand-written load-only loop. It has the same 8 "ldp q" loads per 256 B as the new read kernel. "ldp q" is the Arm instruction that loads two 16-byte vector registers.
test loops of bwx12: the asmread loop with 96 or 256 no-operation instructions per 256 B, and a loop with one load per 64 B line.
the benchmark and its two binaries of 2026-11-13. bw_old was built from the old source, bw_new from the new source.
later runner programs for the same loops. They print one row per thread. bwx12 is the runner of the 2026-11-15 investigation. bwx11 and bwx are older versions.

a process is one start of a benchmark binary. An interval is one timed measurement inside a process. bwx12 times a sequence of kernels and repeats the sequence: each repeat is a round (counted from 0), and the position is the place of a kernel in the sequence (counted from 0). In part A the round (1 or 2) is the round of the script: round 2 runs the processes in the reverse order.
one pass of go.sh through part A, part L and part C.
the driver script of the rerun: three sessions of parts A, L, C and a fourth part C process.
million transfers per second, the unit of memory speed.
a random identifier that Linux creates at each start. Equal boot ids mean the same boot.
1 GB is 1e9 bytes. Every rate is in GB/s.
the 1-minute load average of Linux, read directly before a process starts.
the result file of a part A folder. It holds the output of the benchmark processes of that folder, with one csv line per timed interval. The generator calls such a line an interval row.
the rows of a bwx csv file that hold one thread of one interval each. The generator sums their rates to get the rate of an interval.
the number that a process returns when it ends. 0 means success.
in this test: the case that runs the generator on an unchanged copy of the facts.
lines that make_report.py prints. `STOP` comes with the reason when the script ends early. `FAIL` marks a failed entry of its self-check list.
the two text streams of a process. Normal text goes to the first one, error messages to the second one.

functions.name: run
functions.what: Runs one case: damaged facts copy, patched generator copy, separate process. Prints its `STOP`, `FAIL`, `NOT WRITTEN` and `wrote` lines. Returns the exit status.

functions.name: drop_one
functions.what: Deletes the first part L record of `oldread` and lowers the stored record count by 1.

functions.name: change_a
functions.what: Raises the rate of one part A record of the new read kernel by 5.0 GB/s.

functions.name: change_bwx
functions.what: Raises the rate of the first part C record of kernel `read` by 0.5 GB/s.

functions.name: change_bwx_old
functions.what: Raises the rate of one `B7a` record (runner bwx, kernel `read`, position 6) by 0.5 GB/s.

functions.name: drop_bwx_old
functions.what: Deletes the first `asmread` record of `B5a-rev` and lowers the stored record count by 1.

functions.name: change_10mod
functions.what: Raises the rate of one `X1d10` record (10 memory modules, `asmread`, position 1) by 0.5 GB/s.

functions.name: drop_x2d12
functions.what: Deletes the first `oldread` record at position 0 of `X2d12` and lowers the stored record count by 1.

functions.name: bwx_load
functions.what: Raises the load at launch by 1.0 in every record of one `C3b` process.

functions.name: other_boot
functions.what: Gives the first `asmread` record of control I a boot id of zeros.
